    Co-correspondence analysis

    Source: R/ordination-canoco2.R
    ord_coca.Rd

    CANOCO's co-correspondence analysis (ter Braak and Schaffers 2004; cocorresp::coca()): relates two communities sampled at the same sites, such as plants and insects. The predictive form explains one community (response) from the other (predictor); the symmetric form finds the axes the two share.

    Usage

    ord_coca(
  response,
  predictor,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  method = c("predictive", "symmetric"),
  axes = 2
)

    Arguments

    response, predictor

    Long community data for the two communities.

    site, species, abundance

    Columns, the same in both data sets.

    method

    "predictive" or "symmetric".

    axes

    Number of axes for the predictive form.

    Value

    A list of class td_coca: axes (the variance of the response community explained, predictive; or the eigenvalues, symmetric), sites (site scores of both communities) and fit.

    References

    ter Braak, C. J. F. and Schaffers, A. P. (2004). Co-correspondence analysis: a new ordination method to relate two community compositions. Ecology, 85, 834-846. doi:10.1890/03-0021
